A small forward, Ariza played [[college basketball]] for one season with the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]] before being selected in the second round of the [[2004 NBA draft]] by the [[New York Knicks]]. Ariza won an [[NBA championship]] with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 2009. He also played for the [[Orlando Magic]], [[Houston Rockets]], [[New Orleans Pelicans|New Orleans Hornets]], [[Washington Wizards]], [[Phoenix Suns]], [[Sacramento Kings]], [[Portland Trail Blazers]], and [[Miami Heat]]. ==High school and college career== Ariza attended [[Westchester High School (Los Angeles)|Westchester High School]] in Los Angeles. As a junior in 2001–02, he combined with teammates and fellow future NBA players [[Hassan Adams]], [[Brandon Heath (basketball)|Brandon Heath]], and [[Bobby Brown (basketball)|Bobby Brown]] to lead the Comets to the California State championship. Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Ariza was listed as the No. 5 power forward and the No. 18 player in the nation in 2003.{{Cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/4017|title=Isaiah Foster, 2016 Safety - Rivals.com|website=n.rivals.com}} As a freshman at UCLA in [[2003–04 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2003–04]], Ariza played in 25 games (23 starts) and averaged 11.6 points, 6.5 rebounds and a team-high 1.7 steals. He subsequently earned All-Pac 10 Freshman Team honors. He declared for the NBA Draft following his freshman campaign at UCLA.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/player/2772/trevor-ariza|title=Trevor Ariza | Forward | NBA.com|website=NBA}} ==Professional career== ===New York Knicks (2004–2006)=== Ariza was selected by the [[New York Knicks]] in the second round (43rd overall) of the [[2004 NBA draft]]. At 19 years, four months and four days old, Ariza became the youngest player to ever suit up for the Knicks. In the 2004–2005 season, his 80 games and 1,382 minutes were the most played by a Knicks rookie since [[Greg Anthony]] played 82 games in the 1991–1992 season. Ariza averaged 5.9 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game in his rookie season. ===Orlando Magic (2006–2007)=== In February 2006, Ariza was traded along with [[Penny Hardaway]] to the [[Orlando Magic]] in exchange for [[Steve Francis]]. After the trade, he played in 21 games and averaged 4.7 points per game for the rest of the season. In the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07]] season he played in 57 games and started in 7. He averaged 8.9 [[point (basketball)|point]]s along with 4.4 [[rebounds]] and 1.1 [[assist (basketball)|assist]]s. ===Los Angeles Lakers (2007–2009)=== [[File:Trevor Ariza Lakers.jpg|thumb|upright|Ariza with the Lakers in 2009]] In November 2007, Ariza was traded to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in exchange for [[Brian Cook (basketball)|Brian Cook]] and [[Maurice Evans (basketball)|Maurice Evans]].[http://www.nba.com/magic/news/Magic_Acquire_Brian_Cook_and_M-244872-66.html Magic acquire Cook, Evans from L.A. Lakers] Retrieved November 20, 2007 He fractured a bone in his right foot in January 2008, but made his return in Game 2 of the [[Western Conference (NBA)|Western Conference]] [[NBA Conference Finals|Finals]] against the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in late May, scoring a basket within his first minute of play. The Lakers went on to defeat the Spurs in 5 games and advance to the [[2008 NBA Finals]], but lost to the [[Boston Celtics]] in 6 games. In the [[2008–09 NBA season|2008–09]] season, he played in all 82 games, starting 20. Ariza was ejected during a game against [[Portland Trail Blazers|Portland]] on March 9, 2009, following a [[flagrant foul]] on [[Rudy Fernández (basketball)|Rudy Fernández]].[http://www.latimes.com/sports/basketball/nba/la-sp-lakers-trail-blazers10-2009mar10,0,1112999.story Lakers crash and burn in Portland] Retrieved March 9, 2009 On March 15, 2009, versus the [[Dallas Mavericks]], Ariza scored a career-high 26 points along with 3 steals, 3 rebounds, and 2 assists.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20090315/DALLAL/gameinfo.html?ls=gt1hp0020800991 |title = NBA Games - All NBA matchups {{!}} NBA.com|website = [[NBA.com]]}} After becoming a starter, he began to show more ability on defense.Frank Isola (June 7, 2009). [http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/2009/06/07/2009-06-07_former_knick_trevor_ariza_is_far_from_delusional_in_his_role_with_the_lakers.html "Former Knick Trevor Ariza is far from 'delusional' in his role with Lakers"] ''[[Daily News (New York)]]'' Retrieved on 2009-06-19. In the playoffs, Ariza scored a playoff career-high 21 points in Game 1 of the first round against [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=290419013|title = Jazz vs. Lakers - Box Score - April 19, 2009 - ESPN}} In the Western Conference Finals against the [[Denver Nuggets]], Ariza stole an inbound pass from [[Chauncey Billups]] in Game 1 to help Lakers beat the Nuggets. In Game 3, the Lakers led by two points with 37.1 seconds remaining when Ariza stole [[Kenyon Martin]]'s pass to [[Carmelo Anthony]] near midcourt to help the Lakers take a 2–1 lead.J.A. Adande (May 24, 2009).[https://www.espn.com/nba/dailydime?page=dime-090524 "Nuggets hit by inbound train again"] ''[[ESPN]]'' Retrieved on June 15, 2009. The Lakers won the series 4–2, sending them to the [[NBA Finals]] against the [[Orlando Magic]]. In Game 4 of the [[2009 NBA Finals|Finals]], Ariza, who was 0-for-6 in the first half, scored 13 in the third quarter to help the Lakers win in [[Overtime (sports)|overtime]] and finished the game with nine rebounds and three 3-pointers.Jeff Zillgitt (June 12, 2009).[https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/lakers/2009-06-12-fisher-ariza_N.htm "Fisher, Ariza dazzle Magic in pivotal Game 4"] ''[[USA Today]]'' Retrieved on June 15, 2009. The Lakers went on to win their 15th NBA title in five games, 4–1. Ariza averaged 11.3 points and 4.2 rebounds and shot 50% from three-point range in the playoffs. ===Houston Rockets (2009–2010)=== [[File:Trevor Ariza 2010 vs Suns.jpg|thumb|upright|Ariza playing for the Rockets in 2010]] On July 3, 2009, Ariza reached an agreement with the [[Houston Rockets]] worth $33 million over five years.{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/la-sp-plaschke-lakers3-2009jul03-story.html|title=Lakers move the wrong move going with Ron Artest|date=July 3, 2009|website=Los Angeles Times}} Ariza was signed using the Disabled Player Exception the Rockets were granted for injured center [[Yao Ming]].{{Cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/60432/20090708/rockets_receive_disabled_player_exception_for_yao/|title=Rockets Receive Disabled Player Exception For Yao}} On October 31, 2009, against the Portland Trail Blazers, Ariza scored a career high 33 points in a 111–107 Rockets win. On December 13, 2009, Ariza was ejected after he attempted to punch [[DeMar DeRozan]] of the [[Toronto Raptors]] after having the ball stolen by him. He was subsequently suspended for one game.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4742018&campaign=rss&source=twitter&ex_cid=Twitter_espn_4742018| title=NBA suspends Ariza for one game| access-date=December 25, 2016| website=ESPN.com| author=ESPN news services| date=December 15, 2009}} On April 14, 2010, in the Rockets' final game of the season, Ariza recorded his first career triple-double, tallying 26 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists. ===New Orleans Hornets (2010–2012)=== On August 11, 2010, Ariza was traded to the [[New Orleans Hornets]] as part of a four-team, five-player trade, with [[Darren Collison]] and [[James Posey]] going to the [[Indiana Pacers]], [[Troy Murphy]] to the [[New Jersey Nets]], and [[Courtney Lee]] to Houston.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2010/news/08/11/four.team.trade.ap/index.html?ls=iref:nbahpt1|title=Pacers get Collison from Hornets in 4-team trade|date=August 11, 2010|work=NBA.com|access-date=August 11, 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110530080120/http://www.nba.com/2010/news/08/11/four.team.trade.ap/index.html?ls=iref%3Anbahpt1|archive-date=May 30, 2011}} During the 2011 NBA playoffs, Ariza logged career highs in minutes per game (40.2), points per game (15.5) rebounds (6.5) and assists (3.3). The Hornets lost to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 6 games in the first round. ===Washington Wizards (2012–2014)=== [[File:Trevor Ariza Wizards.jpg|thumb|upright|Ariza with the Wizards in 2013]] On June 20, 2012, Ariza and [[Emeka Okafor]] were traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] for [[Rashard Lewis]] and a draft pick to the New Orleans Hornets.[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards/person-familiar-with-deal-hornets-trade-ariza-okafor-to-wizards-for-lewis-2nd-round-pick/2012/06/20/gJQAc77mqV_story.html Hornets trade Trevor Ariza, Emeka Okafor to Wizards for Rashard Lewis, 2nd-round pick]{{dead link|date=June 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} On February 12, 2014, Ariza recorded a career-high 10 made three-pointers to score a season-high 32 points, as well as 11 rebounds, 3 assists and 3 steals, in a 113–112 loss to the Houston Rockets.[http://www.nba.com/games/20140212/WASHOU/gameinfo.html Notebook: Rockets 113, Wizards 112] The 10 three-pointers set a franchise record for most made three-pointers in a game.{{cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2025/11/24/wizards-scores-schedule-highlights-and-transactions/|title=CJ McCollum’s Wizards crush the Hawks to snap their 14-game skid|work=washingtonpost.com|date=November 25, 2025|access-date=November 26, 2025}} On March 1, 2014, Ariza recorded a career-high 40 points, including eight 3-pointers, in a 122–103 victory over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|last=Jasner|first=Andy|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140301/WASPHI/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Wizards 122, Sixers 103|work=NBA.com|date=March 1, 2014|access-date=March 2, 2014}} On April 27, 2014, Ariza set a playoff career-high 30 points against the [[Chicago Bulls]] in Game 4 of their [[2014 NBA Playoffs]] first-round match-up, which the Wizards won 98–89. The team went on to lose to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in six games in the conference semifinals. ===Return to Houston (2014–2018)=== On July 15, 2014, Ariza was re-acquired by the Houston Rockets in a three-team sign-and-trade deal that also involved the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], which sent [[Ömer Aşık|Omer Asik]] and [[Omri Casspi]] to the Pelicans, [[Melvin Ely]] to the Wizards, and Ariza, along with [[Alonzo Gee]] and [[Scotty Hopson]], to the Rockets.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/rockets-land-ariza-three-team-deal|title=Rockets Land Ariza & Valuable First Round Pick|work=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2014|access-date=July 15, 2014}} On February 6, 2015, he tied a season-high with 24 points in a 117–111 win. This was during a streak of 172 straight games played.[http://www.nba.com/games/20151212/LALHOU/gameinfo.html Harden leads Rockets to lopsided 126–97 win over Lakers] On January 24, 2016, he scored a season-high 29 points and made a season-high six three-pointers in a 115–104 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20160124/DALHOU/gameinfo.html Harden's triple-double leads Rockets over Mavericks 115–104] He topped that mark the following night, scoring 31 points in a 112–111 win over the New Orleans Pelicans.[http://www.nba.com/games/20160125/HOUNOP/gameinfo.html Harden and Ariza lead Rockets to 112–111 win over Pelicans] On February 27, he made two three-pointers against the San Antonio Spurs to extend his streak with at least one three-pointer to 29 games, the longest streak by a Rockets player since 39 in a row by [[Aaron Brooks (basketball)|Aaron Brooks]] in the 2009–10 season.[http://www.nba.com/games/20160227/SASHOU/gameinfo.html Leonard leads Spurs to 50th win, 104–94 over Rockets] The streak ended at 30 after shooting 0-of-8 from three-point range against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] on March 2.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/arizatr01/gamelog/2016/|title=Trevor Ariza 2015-16 Game Log|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} On January 17, 2018, Ariza was suspended for two games without pay for entering the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]' locker room after a game against the team two days earlier.{{Cite web |title=Rockets' Trevor Ariza and Gerald Green suspended two games |url=https://pr.nba.com/rockets-ariza-green-suspended-two-games/ |access-date=November 21, 2022 |website=NBA|date=January 18, 2018 }} In Game 2 of the [[2018 NBA Playoffs|2018 Western Conference Finals]], on May 17, 2018, Ariza helped tie the series with 19 points and 6 assists in a 127–105 victory over the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/gametracker/recap/NBA_20180516_GS@HOU/|title = Golden State Warriors vs. Houston Rockets Live Score and Stats - May 16, 2018 Gametracker}} In Game 7 of the signed a one-year, $15 million contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-trevor-ariza|title=Suns Sign Trevor Ariza, 14-year veteran and NBA Champion|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2018|access-date=July 6, 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23958932/phoenix-suns-agree-one-year-deal-trevor-ariza|title=Suns agree to Score|work=ESPN.com|date=October 17, 2018|access-date=October 17, 2018}} ===Return to Washington (2018–2019)=== On December 17, 2018, Ariza was traded to the Washington Wizards for [[Austin Rivers]] and [[Kelly Oubre Jr.]]{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-acquire-trevor-ariza-trade-oubre-rivers-suns|title=Wizards acquire Trevor Ariza|work=NBA.com|date=December 17, 2018|access-date=December 17, 2018}} On January 13, 2019, he narrowly missed his second career triple-double, recording 23 points, 10 assists and nine rebounds in a 140–138 double-overtime loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071315|title=Ibaka's 3-pointer helps Raptors survive Wizards in double OT|work=ESPN.com|date=January 13, 2019|access-date=January 13, 2019}} ===Sacramento Kings (2019–2020)=== On July 7, 2019, Ariza inked a two-year deal worth $25 million with the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2819492-trevor-ariza-kings-reportedly-agree-on-2-year-25m-contract-in-free-agency|title=Trevor Ariza, Kings Reportedly Agree on 2-Year, $25M Contract in web|url=https://www.nba.com/game/gsw-vs-sac-0021900547?watch |title=Golden State Warriors vs Sacramento Kings Jan 6, 2020 Game - Scores, Stats & Highlights |work=NBA.com |date= |accessdate=2022-09-10}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2020)=== On January 20, 2020, Ariza was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] along with [[Wenyen Gabriel]] and [[Caleb Swanigan]] in exchange for future teammate [[Kent Bazemore]], [[Anthony Tolliver]], and two future second-round draft picks.{{cite web |title=Trail Blazers Acquire Trevor Ariza, Wenyen Gabriel, and Caleb Swanigan from Sacramento |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2020/1/20/trail-blazers-acquire-trevor-ariza-wenyen-gabriel-caleb-swanigan-from-sacramento |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 21, 2020 |date=January 20, 2020}} On June 22, 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, Ariza announced he would not be returning to the NBA season's restart in Orlando. Instead, he committed to a one-month visitation window with his young son, sources told [[ESPN]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29349415/sources-blazers-trevor-ariza-opting-participation-nba-orlando-restart|title=Sources: Ariza opts out of NBA restart to visit son|date=June 22, 2020}} On November 22, 2020, Ariza, the draft rights to [[Isaiah Stewart]], and a conditional future first-round pick were traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for [[Robert Covington]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2020/11/22/blazers-acquire-robert-covington|title=TRAIL BLAZERS ACQUIRE ROBERT COVINGTON FROM HOUSTON|work=NBA.com|date=November 22, 2020}} On November 24, Ariza and Stewart were traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for [[Christian Wood]], as part of a sign-and-trade deal.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-complete-trade-houston|title=Detroit Pistons Complete Trade With Houston|work=NBA.com|date=November 24, 2020|access-date=November 25, 2020}} On November 27, Ariza, [[Justin Jackson (basketball, born 1995)|Justin Jackson]], a 2023 second-round pick (from either Dallas or Miami), and a 2026 second-round pick were traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/acquisitions-201127|title=Thunder Acquires Trevor Ariza, Justin Jackson and Two Second-Round Draft Picks|work=NBA.com|date=November 27, 2020}} Ariza never reported to the Thunder or appeared in any games for them during his stint, as he was away from the team due to family matters.{{cite web |title=Trevor Ariza away from Thunder indefinitely (family) |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2020/12/07/trevor-ariza-away-from-thunder-indefinitely-family/ |access-date=March 14, 2022 Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} ===Return to the Lakers (2021–2022)=== On August 6, 2021, Ariza signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Trevor Ariza|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-trevor-ariza-2021|website=NBA.com|date=August 6, 2021|access-date=August 6, 2021}} on a one-year deal worth $2.6 million.{{cite web|title=Trevor Ariza NBA Salary - How much is he making?|url=https://hoopshype.com/player/trevor-ariza/salary/|website=HoopsHype.com}} On October 6, he underwent a procedure on his right ankle.{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Feldman|title=Lakers: Trevor Ariza out eight weeks with ankle injury|url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2021/10/06/lakers-trevor-ariza-out-eight-weeks-with-ankle-injury/|website=NBCSports.com|date=October 6, 2022|access-date=March 14, 2022 }} He was out for most of the first half, which Lakers head coach [[Frank Vogel]] said "did derail most of his season and his impact on our team this year".{{cite news|first=Dan|last=Woike|title=Talen Horton-Tucker scores 40 as Lakers' stars get front-row seats to another loss|date=April 7, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/story/2022-04-07/lakers-golden-state-warriors-lebron-james-nba-trevor-ariza|access-date=April 8, 2022}} On April 7, 2022, Ariza was waived.{{cite web|title=Lakers Waive Trevor Ariza|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-waive-trevor-ariza-4-7-22|website=NBA.com|date=April 7, 2022|access-date=April 7, 2022}} He played in 24 games with 11 starts, averaging four points and shooting 33.3%. ==Personal life== On March 18, 1996, Ariza's youngest brother, Tajh Ariza, died at age six after falling out of a hotel room window in [[Caracas]], [[Venezuela]].{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/draft/2004-06-24-ariza_x.htm|date=June 24, 2004|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090227125822/https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/draft/2004-06-24-ariza_x.htm|access-date=December 3, 2025|title=UCLA's Ariza moves from tragedy to prospect|archive-date=February 27, 2009}} Ariza's older son [[Tajh Ariza|Tajh]], named after Ariza's late brother, is a five-star basketball prospect and one of the top recruits in the class of 2026.{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/oregon/football/oregon-ducks-recruit-tajh-ariza-visiting-son-nba-star-trevor-ariza-los-angeles-lakers-dana-altman-jackson-shelstad-nate-bittle|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=5-Star Recruit Tajh Ariza Visiting Oregon Ducks, Son of L.A. Lakers Star Trevor Ariza|date=May 26, 2025|author=Dimmitt, Zach}} Ariza also has two children with his wife: son Tristan and daughter Taylor.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29734146/afar-watching-lakers-blazers-trevor-ariza|title = From afar, watching Lakers-Blazers with Trevor Ariza|date = August 25, 2020}} As of 2020, Ariza had a foundation, Choices Mentoring program, which helps young African Americans work toward their professional goals by providing access to tutoring, scholarships, and counselors. Ariza's stepfather, Kenny McClary, played at the [[University of Florida]] in the mid to late 1980s, and professionally with the [[Sydney Kings]] in Australia. Ariza is of [[Turks and Caicos Islands]] and [[Dominican Republic|Dominican]] descent through his grandfather Osvaldo Ariza (a Turks and Caicos Islander of [[People of the Dominican
